cards.subject: The great multitude of Revelation 7:9 before the throne and the Lamb, composed for the arched window as a golden heaven. At the top centre, in a round glory of gold light, the white Lamb of God standing on a small green mount from which four streams flow, with a plain gold halo and a small white banner bearing a red cross (no lettering). Around and below him, on tiers of soft white cloud that curve like an amphitheatre, the saints half-length and small, all in white robes or in their own dress, many holding green palm branches: nearest the Lamb, Our Lady in her blue mantle with hands joined; St. Peter with his keys and St. Paul with his sword; martyrs with palms; virgins with white lilies; a bishop in a white mitre; a king with a simple gold crown laid at his breast; a brown-habited friar; a mother and a young shepherd boy; men and women of Africa, Asia and the Americas in their own dress. Everyone's face turns toward the Lamb, joyful and at peace. At the very bottom, a thin band of green earth with a small village church under a clear morning sky. Keep every cloud and figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; she is nearest the Lamb, looking up. Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; Paul as on the paul card: about sixty, a noble LONG face — a high domed forehead, bald on top with dark wavy hair greying at the sides, a straight fine nose, calm luminous dark eyes, a long dark pointed beard streaked with grey reaching well below the chin; both small, on the tier below Our Lady. The rest of the multitude is small and deliberately varied: a young Roman virgin with a round face and dark braided hair; a tall, lean East African martyr with a long face and close-cropped hair; a round-faced Japanese youth with straight black hair; an old bishop with a square face and white beard; a Brazilian mother with warm brown skin and a broad smile; a freckled boy with straw-coloured hair.
cards.basis: The feast's own reading and the formulary description point to Revelation 7:9, the multitude before the throne and the Lamb; the tiered heaven of saints follows Fra Angelico's Fiesole predella and Dürer's Landauer Altarpiece, with the Lamb and the four rivers of the Ghent Altarpiece.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Fiesole Altarpiece (Fra Angelico)
Wikipedia, Landauer Altarpiece (Dürer, Adoration of the Trinity)
Wikipedia, All Saints' Day

cards.subject: A quiet country churchyard at dusk on the evening of All Souls, peaceful and hopeful, with no skulls, no bones and no dark or frightening imagery. In the lower half, a widow in a dark shawl kneels half-length at a grave marked by a plain wooden cross (no inscription), a rosary in her joined hands, her young son beside her setting down a lit candle; around them other graves with plain stone crosses, glowing votive candles in small glass lanterns, pots of white and golden chrysanthemums, two dark cypresses and the lit doorway of a small whitewashed chapel with a bell-cote. In the upper half, the deep blue-violet evening sky opens into a soft rose-gold glow: a tall angel in white and pale gold robes, wings spread, bends down to take by the hand a soul in a plain white robe, a grey-haired man with joined hands, and lifts him gently upward toward the light, while a few other souls in white, small, wait calmly with hands joined, looking up with hope amid low, gentle rose-gold light like the last of the sunset. Keep the churchyard and the sky inside the arched window.
cards.face: The angel: youthful and serene, a HEART-SHAPED face with a broad smooth brow tapering to a small pointed chin, wide-set grey-blue eyes, a fine straight nose, fair skin and short golden hair curling at the ears; a gentle, consoling smile. The soul being raised: a man of about seventy with a SQUARE face, a broad nose, deep smile-lines and short grey hair, clean-shaven, his face lit with relief. The widow: about forty, a LONG, narrow face with a high-bridged nose, dark brows and dark eyes lowered in prayer, dark hair under her shawl. The boy: about eight, a ROUND freckled face and tousled brown hair.
cards.basis: The card keeps both images the brief allows: the churchyard on the night of 2 November, with candles and flowers as the faithful still do, and above it an angel leading a soul out of purgatory, a common theme of Catholic altar paintings of the souls, painted here as consolation, not torment.

sources.title: Wikipedia, All Souls' Day
Wikipedia, Purgatory

cards.subject: The Archbasilica of the Most Holy Saviour and St. John Lateran in Rome, its east façade by Alessandro Galilei seen from the piazza in warm late-afternoon light: a single giant order of paired Corinthian pilasters and half-columns in pale golden travertine, five tall arched openings of the portico below and the benediction loggia above, the central bay projecting under a triangular pediment, and along the balustrade the fifteen colossal white statues, the Saviour at the centre holding his cross, St. John the Baptist and St. John the Evangelist on either side, and the Doctors of the Church in their robes, mitres and hats beyond. The pediment and frieze are plain, with no inscription. The great bronze central doors stand open onto the candlelit gold of the nave. Small figures on the wide steps: a priest in a white surplice and violet stole greeting a family of pilgrims, two nuns, a boy with a candle. Clear sky with a few gold-edged clouds and swallows. Keep the whole façade inside the arched window.
cards.face: The figures are small and secondary: the priest, about sixty, a lean, NARROW face, clean-shaven, silver hair, turned in three-quarter view; the pilgrim father, about thirty-five, a broad, ruddy face with a short brown beard; his wife with a round face under a light scarf; the boy, about ten, dark-haired, looking up at the statues. The statues are white stone, not living people.
cards.basis: The Lateran is the Pope's cathedral, the 'mother and head of all churches of the City and the world'. The card paints Galilei's façade of 1735 with its fifteen statues, Christ the Saviour between the two Johns and the Doctors of the Church, as the basilica's own website and guides describe it.

sources.title: Basilica of St. John Lateran, Façade and Loggias
Wikipedia, Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran

cards.subject: Sts. Peter and Paul half-length side by side, each holding on his arm a small model of the basilica built over his tomb, as founders do in old altarpieces. Peter (left), turned a little right, in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, his keys hanging from his right hand, holds on his left forearm a model of St. Peter's with Michelangelo's great ribbed dome and Maderno's façade. Paul (right), turned a little left, in a green tunic and a deep red mantle, a long sword resting point-down against his shoulder, holds a model of St. Paul Outside the Walls: its long basilica roof, the gabled façade glinting with gold mosaic, the square campanile and the colonnaded courtyard with palm trees. Behind them, Rome at sunset along the Tiber: the dome of St. Peter's far off at the left, umbrella pines, bridges and ochre roofs, the Aventine hill at the right. No lettering on the models. Keep both models inside the arched window.
cards.face: Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a steady, fatherly gaze toward the viewer. Paul as on the paul card: about sixty, a noble LONG face — a high domed forehead, bald on top with dark wavy hair greying at the sides, a straight fine nose, calm luminous dark eyes, a long dark pointed beard streaked with grey reaching well below the chin; eyes lifted, thoughtful. The two faces must stay clearly different: Peter broad, square-bearded and grey-white; Paul long, bald-domed and dark-bearded.
cards.basis: The feast keeps the dedications of the Vatican basilica and of St. Paul's on the Via Ostiense, both built over the Apostles' tombs; showing each Apostle carrying his church follows the founder-with-model convention and the recognisable forms of the two buildings. Faces and dress continue the `peter` and `paul` cards.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
Wikipedia, St. Peter's Basilica

cards.subject: Our Lady half-length and close, holding the newborn Child in white swaddling bands upright against her shoulder, his cheek pressed to hers and one small hand at her neck, her hand cradling his back: the tender embrace of the Virgin of Tenderness (Eleousa), painted in the card's own style. Her eyes are lowered, pondering. She wears her blue mantle over the white veil and a rose-red gown. Behind them the rock-hewn stable of Bethlehem, a manger with straw and the dim head of an ox in the shadow at the left, and through the rough stone opening at the right the terraced hills of Bethlehem and a few sleeping sheep under the first pale gold light of a winter dawn, a single bright star fading in the sky. Keep the stable opening inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; her lids lowered, her cheek against the Child's. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo; eight days old, eyes open and resting on his mother.
cards.basis: The solemnity closes the octave of Christmas, and its gospel ends with Mary pondering these things in her heart. The embrace follows the Theotokos of Vladimir, the classic image of the Mother of God, so this card differs from the manger of `nativity_christ` and the enthroned Child of `epiphany`.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Theotokos of Vladimir
Wikipedia, Mary, mother of God

cards.subject: The house and workshop of Nazareth in the warm light of late afternoon, three figures half-length side by side. St. Joseph (left) at his carpenter's bench, a plane in his hand, pausing to look down with love; the boy Jesus (centre), about seven, in a simple rose-red tunic, carrying a small plank of fresh wood toward him, curled shavings at his feet; Our Lady (right), seated, spinning white wool with a distaff and looking up at them both with a quiet smile. On the wall hang saws and a mallet; a clay water jar and a loaf on a low shelf; a white dove on the window sill. Through the open doorway, the flat-roofed white houses of Nazareth climbing a green hillside with olive trees and a few cypresses under a clear sky. Keep the workshop and the doorway inside the arched window.
cards.face: St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; a green tunic and an ochre-brown mantle. The boy Jesus: the Christ Child's face as in recurring-figures.md, lengthened to about seven — a softly rounded face with full cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small straight nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, golden-brown curls to the ears, a plain gold halo; an eager, trusting look up at Joseph. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about twenty-five with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head.
cards.basis: The hidden life at Nazareth (Lk 2:39-40, 51-52) in the tradition of the carpenter's workshop, as in Murillo's Holy Family with a Little Bird and the many workshop scenes of the Holy Family, with the three faces kept from the recurring figures.

cards.subject: Christ standing in the shallow Jordan, seen from the waist up, bare-shouldered and modest, the water about his waist, head gently bowed and hands joined at his breast. St. John the Baptist stands on the rocky bank at the right in his camel-hair tunic and red mantle, pouring water over Christ's head from a scallop shell, a slender reed cross in the crook of his other arm. At the left two small kneeling angels on the bank hold Christ's rose-red tunic and blue mantle ready. Above, the heavens open in a burst of gold between clouds and the white dove of the Holy Spirit descends in a shaft of light. Around them green reeds and tamarisks along the river, the bare hills of the Judaean wilderness beyond in soft morning light. Keep the dove, the angels and the bank inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; eyes lowered in humility. John as on the john_baptist card: a man of about thirty with a LONG face — high cheekbones, a straight nose, large dark-brown eyes under straight dark brows, a firm mouth; thick, unkempt curly dark-brown hair to the shoulders and a rough, short dark-brown beard, sunburnt wilderness skin; a reverent look. The two must stay clearly different: Christ's hair smooth, chestnut and centre-parted, John's dark, wild and curly. The angels: fair, childlike, one round-faced with golden curls, one with an oval face and light-brown hair.
cards.basis: Matthew 3:13-17 and the feast's entrance antiphon; the composition follows Verrocchio and Leonardo's Baptism of Christ (Uffizi), with John pouring from a shell and angels holding the garments. John keeps the `john_baptist` card's face and Christ the new line in recurring-figures.md.

cards.subject: The risen Christ standing before the open rock-hewn tomb at sunrise, seen to the knees, radiant in a white robe and white mantle, a soft golden light around him; his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding the white banner of victory with a red cross on a slender gold cross-staff (no lettering); the wounds only small, clean marks on his hands. Behind him the round millstone rolled aside from the dark doorway of the tomb, and a young angel in white seated on the stone. At the lower right, small, two Roman soldiers asleep against the rock with their shields, faces turned away. A garden of white lilies and olive trees, and on the horizon the walls and towers of Jerusalem under a rose-gold dawn sky. Keep the tomb and the soldiers inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; in glory, a plain gold halo ringed with rays, a serene, victorious look straight out at the viewer. The angel: youthful, an OVAL face with a straight nose, fair skin and loose light-golden hair, looking toward Christ. The soldiers' faces are hidden.
cards.basis: The Gospel accounts of the empty tomb (Mt 28:1-6, Jn 20:1) with the Western image of the risen Christ holding the banner of victory, as in Carl Bloch's Resurrection; Christ keeps the line from `transfiguration`.

sources.title: Commons, Carl Heinrich Bloch, The Resurrection (1873)

cards.subject: In the upper half, Christ rising on a bright cloud above the summit of the Mount of Olives, in a white robe and white-gold mantle, both hands raised in blessing, the wounds only small, clean marks on his palms, in a glory of gold light. In the lower half, gathered on the hilltop and looking up in wonder, half-length: Our Lady in the centre with hands joined, St. Peter at the left in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, St. John at the right in his green tunic and red-orange mantle, and a few other Apostles behind them; two angels in white stand at the sides, one pointing upward. Olive trees around them, and far below the walls of Jerusalem and the Temple mount in clear afternoon light. Keep the cloud and all figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; in glory, a plain gold halo ringed with rays, a serene, loving look down on his disciples. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: the same face matured, a woman of about fifty with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard. John as on the john_evangelist card: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw. The other Apostles behind, small and different: a dark-bearded man of forty with a long face (James), a grey-bearded older man with a broad face (Andrew), a young man with short black hair and a narrow, beardless face (Thomas). The angels: youthful, fair, oval-faced.
cards.basis: Acts 1:9-11, the entrance antiphon's 'Men of Galilee', and the traditional Ascension with Our Lady among the Apostles (Giotto, Scrovegni Chapel). Christ keeps the line from `transfiguration`; Peter and John keep the `peter` and `john_evangelist` faces; Our Lady matured.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Ascension of Jesus in Christian art

cards.subject: The Upper Room in Jerusalem on the morning of Pentecost: Our Lady seated at the centre, half-length, hands joined, eyes raised, with the Apostles gathered close around her, their mantles stirred by a rushing wind; above each head, Mary's included, a small, clear tongue of golden flame. Over her, the white dove of the Holy Spirit spreads its wings in a burst of golden light that fills the room. St. Peter at her right in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, hands open; St. John at her left in his green tunic and red-orange mantle, hand on his heart; the other Apostles behind them in varied colours, some raising their hands, one bowing. A plain stone room with a round arch and a small window showing the flat roofs of Jerusalem in morning light. Keep the dove and all figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: the same face matured, a woman of about fifty with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; eyes raised, radiant. Peter as on the peter card: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard. John as on the john_evangelist card: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw. The others behind, each different: a dark-bearded man of forty with a long face (James); a grey-bearded older man with a broad face and short hair (Andrew); a young man with short black hair and a narrow, beardless face (Thomas); a bald man of fifty with a round face and a short brown beard (Bartholomew).
cards.basis: Acts 2:1-4, with Our Lady at the centre as in Acts 1:14 and the Western Pentecost (El Greco, Prado); Peter and John keep the `peter` and `john_evangelist` faces, Our Lady matured.
